title: Microsoft 2026 Annual Shareholders Meeting — the first governance venue after the two-segment recast
source: EST: the date is read VERBATIM FROM A PRIMARY SEC FILING and the estimate label is about the proposal mechanism, not the evidence. Microsoft's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 2026-06-30 (SEC accession 0001193125-26-323660, filed 2026-07-29, primary document msft-20260630.htm, fetched direct from sec.gov and text-extracted 2026-09-09) states on its cover page, under DOCUMENTS INCORPORATED BY REFERENCE: 'Portions of the definitive Proxy Statement to be delivered to shareholders in connection with the Annual Meeting of Shareholders to be held on December 8, 2026 are incorporated by reference into Part III', and restates it in Part III Item 10: 'our Proxy Statement for the Annual Meeting of Shareholders to be held December 8, 2026'. TWO MECHANICAL REASONS THIS CANNOT BE FILED CONFIRMED, neither of which is doubt about the date: (1) a proposal is ALWAYS status estimate (docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md adjacency-sweep rule, issue #1717) — a sibling lane's find never self-confirms; (2) scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs allows an estimate only an EST:/NEWS: prefix, so the SEC: prefix this evidence would otherwise justify is unavailable at this status. Cadence corroboration, independent of the filing: Microsoft's 2025 annual meeting was held 2025-12-05 and the meeting has landed in the first half of December in each recent year. PROMOTION CRITERION: the definitive DEF 14A proxy statement (historically filed mid-to-late October) naming 2026-12-08, or a microsoft.com/en-us/investor/annual-meeting page stating it — either flips this to confirmed on a SEC:/IR: prefix. Discovered 2026-09-09 during the msft-2026-10-27-print adjacency sweep
notes: PROPOSED by the msft-2026-10-27-print pulse check (2026-09-09, D-48) as the second MSFT-specific catalyst after the FY27-Q1 print (est. 2026-10-27) and roughly three weeks past Microsoft Ignite (msft-ignite-2026-11-17, estimate). WHY IT EARNS A ROW: it is the first annual meeting held under the two-segment reporting structure the 2026-09-02 8-K announced (Agents and Infra / Devices and Consumer), so the shareholder-proposal slate and the board's own framing of AI capex land after investors have seen exactly one quarter of standalone dollar Azure disclosure — and FY27-Q1 capex alone is guided 'over $50 billion'. The proxy that precedes it (DEF 14A, historically mid-to-late October) is the document that actually carries the proposals, and it is due in the same window as the print. WHY IMPACT IS LOW AND WHY NOTHING KEYS ON IT: an annual meeting is a governance calendar item, not a print — no consensus number, no scheduled surprise, no release time to trade around; docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md carry no annual-meeting or governance-keyed hypothesis, so no house playbook fires here. KIND IS AN HONEST APPROXIMATION: scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs's KINDS list has no company-governance slot, and 'sector' is the list's catch-all for a scheduled structural event that is neither an earnings print nor a product launch (the market-closure entries use it the same way); 'product-launch' would be a worse fit than the imprecision. ATTRIBUTION TRAP, stated now rather than later: 2026-12-08 sits inside the December macro block, so any MSFT move that session has a macro explanation before it has a governance one. Every statement keyed to this date inherits the estimate label.
